title: Light Speed Stop 9: Voyager 1 Escaped
topic: Light-speed journey stop 9: interstellar space and Voyager 1 (left heliosphere 2012; launched 1977; ~1 light-day away; ~17 km/s; golden record; Proxima Centauri ~4.2 light-years, Proxima b in habitable zone)
links_to_previous: Answers episode 8's cliffhanger (has anything human-made left the solar system?): yes, Voyager 1. The journey continues into interstellar space toward the nearest star.
hook: Yes. One machine has already escaped.
cliffhanger_question: Could the planet at our nearest star hold life? Yes or no?
summary: Answer: yes, Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in 2012. Launched in 1977, it is about one light-day away, moving ~17 km/s, and still talks to Earth. Even so, the nearest star is about 70,000 years away at that speed. Next stop: Proxima Centauri.

scenes.narration: Yes. One machine has already escaped.
Voyager One left the Sun's bubble in twenty twelve.
Launched in nineteen seventy-seven, it's still talking to Earth.
It's now about one light-day away. A radio signal takes twenty-four hours.
Its computers hold less memory than a single photo on your phone.
It carries a golden record with greetings, music, and sounds of Earth.
Out here, the Sun is just another bright star.
It flies about seventeen kilometers every second.
Even at that speed, the nearest star is about seventy thousand years away.
Light makes that trip in just over four years.
That star, Proxima Centauri, has a planet in its habitable zone.
